A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M2-REPA study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original RealEstate10K and Minecraft experiments, qualitative generations, component ablations, and cross-source supervision tests.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds OmniWorld-Game evaluation and experiments using TesserAct with a CogVideoX-5B backbone.

M1.justification: The modality-specific MLP projections, frozen foundation experts, cosine alignment, CKA decoupling, and flow-matching objective remain unchanged. Appendix G applies the existing recipe to TesserAct without documenting a new algorithmic component or procedure.

E1.justification: New Appendix F reports retraining and evaluation on OmniWorld-Game, previously only cited, with engine-rendered depth and independently produced full-scene instance masks. This extends game-data coverage within the existing multimodal generation task. RealEstate10K and Minecraft remain; the TesserAct experiment reuses RealEstate10K.

E2.justification: TesserAct becomes an actually evaluated baseline in new Table G.1, alongside single-teacher and naive multi-expert REPA variants. Previously it was discussed and cited but not quantitatively compared. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added experiments substantially extend evaluation conditions: Appendix F introduces 200-frame evaluation using engine-rendered depth and full-scene GroundingDINO+SAM mask references, while Appendix G evaluates a TesserAct/CogVideoX-5B configuration. These are additional settings; the original training budgets, preprocessing, metrics, and rollout protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F strengthens the existing supervision-bias investigation with engine-rendered depth and independently annotated masks, beyond v1's Video-Depth-Anything cross-source test. Appendix G adds a targeted test of applicability to a 5B-parameter generator. Together these substantially extend robustness and scaling analyses; the earlier component, projection-head, alignment-layer, and loss-weight ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without specifying repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The new tables follow the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables F.1 and G.1 add results for independent annotations and a large-model configuration. Within these new comparisons, M2-REPA reports FVD 157.4 versus 217.0 for the OmniWorld-Game RGB-DM baseline, and 418.3 versus 639.3 for TesserAct. Table F.1 shows a mixed depth finding: M2-REPA's delta1 is 0.124 versus 0.127 for naive multi-expert REPA. Retained tables and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, losses, mask metric, and CKA definition and properties are unchanged. Appendix E uses equivalent mask-set notation, and the relocated CKA appendix corrects a cross-reference from Equation 6 to Equation 7 without changing mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claim and contributions: multimodal representation alignment through expert-specific decoupling, complementary priors, and improved generation across backbones. Removing emphatic wording does not change these claims' scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets the independent-reference results as evidence against alignment/evaluation coupling, and Appendix G extends the applicability discussion to 5B models. Existing limitations remain unchanged. Appendix F's claim of improvements across the listed metrics overstates Table F.1, where delta1 does not improve.

D1.justification: The new experiments identify annotation provenance and the TesserAct/CogVideoX-5B backbone. However, their experiment-specific training budgets, splits, and other implementation settings are not detailed. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, VAE, initialization, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 modestly qualifies prior-work positioning: methods previously described as strictly confined to RGB generation are now largely confined to it and typically use isolated foundation models. The same 65 cited works remain; bibliography capitalization, metadata, and access-date edits do not add research coverage.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, reduces promotional language, expands affiliation information, and adds acknowledgements. References move after the appendices, and new appendices F and G precede the retained CKA material, now Appendix H. The main narrative and section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables F.1 and G.1, enlarges or reformats architecture diagrams, adjusts qualitative-figure sizing, and changes Figure 5's colors and proportions while retaining its data. Appendix displays receive section-based numbering, and page layouts are reflowed. Existing visual examples and table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The independent-reference experiment and 5B-model comparison strengthen evidence for robustness and scalability beyond v1's existing evaluations. Wording and diagram refinements also help presentation. The improvement is limited by sparse setup details for the new experiments and Appendix F's inaccurate claim of gains across all listed metrics, despite its unchanged or worse delta1 results.
